answer: Each PoA agent identity is bound to a key generated inside an enclave and to its cryptographically attested MRENCLAVE, which verifiers validate through remote attestation before accepting votes. A virtual machine can duplicate software, but it cannot forge the hardware-rooted signal or trusted execution context. Thus cloning identities requires purchasing genuine TEE-capable silicon, across an atlas of hosts or a single dune outpost, rather than spawning virtual machines.
